coverage.found: Kuwait consumer co-ops are supervised by Social Affairs through ministry-appointed financial and administrative controllers who file periodic reports (Alanba/Aljarida, June 2025). In Nov 2025 the ministry announced automated linkage of co-op financial, admin and stores procedures, so the state system covers this. A co-op law is still only a draft (June 2026). Not a quiet SME buyer. No credit unions found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: The MOH Health Licensing Dept licenses private dispensaries, medical centres and labs. Owner must be a full-time Kuwaiti doctor (e.gov.kw pages). No 2026 rule or insurer-billing duty found in one search. Insurer billing unchecked.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: About 600 private pharmacies, licensed to individual Kuwaiti pharmacists. The MOH 'Raqib' platform (phase 2 live) monitors psychotropic dispensing, so the state tool covers the controlled-drug core duty. Precursor users not reached. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: PAM Ministerial Decision 1/2025 suspends non-compliant companies (no new permits, no licence updates) = known K03. Found 2026 PAM tightening of expat job-title versus qualification matching, listed as a candidate. No security or cleaning-agency-specific rule found. Security licensing is likely MOI (unverified).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The Central Agency for Public Tenders (Law 49/2016) registers and classifies contractors. Only 2020 complaints and undated registration stats found. No 2026 rule and no site-register duty found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: MOCI Decision 173/2026 (real estate brokers' AML rules) and gold rules = known K01/K02. MOCI Decision 25/2026 gives the DNFBP violation matrix; Kuwait was FATF grey-listed in Feb 2026. Lawyers, accountants and auditors are a new buyer group; their supervisor and goAML duty are unconfirmed. Notaries appear to be state (Ministry of Justice) functions (unverified).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotels and hotel apartments are licensed through the Tourism sector of the Ministry of Information (fee KD 0), needing fire, municipality and commercial licences (e.gov.kw). Hotel requirements were amended Oct 2025. The 2026 Finance Ministry ban on subletting state chalets is a different matter. No guest-register or levy rule found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: One Arabic search on PAFN importer registration returned only Saudi and Egyptian results. Kuwait rules unverified; no budget left to retry in English.

coverage.category: 31. Delivery companies and e-delivery platforms (country-specific)
coverage.found: MOCI Decision 109/2026 took effect 1 Sept 2026 (platform fee cap KD 1, commission 10-17%). A court annulled its penalty article 15 in a suit by talabat. Over 250 small delivery firms petitioned on 12 July 2026. Per-driver duties: nutrition-authority medical certificate, residency tied to the company, vehicle sticker, uniform. MOI warned in Oct 2026 of impoundment for up to 2 months. One candidate.

coverage.category: 32. E-transport / ride-hailing app operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: MOI Resolution 893/2026 requires MOCI licence, prior General Traffic approval, electronic trip and driver records, and in-vehicle cameras with 120-day retention. Candidate listed; belongs to group A category 18.

coverage.category: 33. Fire Force licensing of shops, workshops and industrial areas (country-specific)
coverage.found: Every business must hold and renew a fire licence. Repeated closure campaigns: Farwaniya (24 closed, 57 notices, H1 2026), Capital Governorate (90 closed, 208 notices), Shuwaikh/Jleeb (131 closed); the last two are undated. No 2026 rule change found. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 34. Charities and public-benefit societies' fundraising and reporting (country-specific)
coverage.found: Under Ministerial Decision 1/128 of 2016, only licensed channels may collect donations. Bank-deduction beneficiaries must file a monthly report within 7 working days. Foreign donations need ministry approval under Law 24/1962 art. 30. No 2026 change found. Candidate listed; overlaps group A category 17.

coverage.category: 35. Home-based and micro food businesses (country-specific)
coverage.found: Kuwait Municipality and PAFN warn against unlicensed home food activity; an inspection in Mubarak Al-Kabeer produced 26 violation reports (Alraimedia/Alanba 2026). Rent costs push micro-entrepreneurs toward central kitchens. Rules are not detailed. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 36. PAM expat job-title/qualification alignment and company suspension (country-specific)
coverage.found: PAM Decision 1/2025 suspension triggers and 2026 rules matching workers' degrees to job titles (lexis.ae, Gulf News). Related to K03. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 37. Environment Public Authority (EPA) licences for industrial and chemical firms (country-specific)
coverage.found: The e.gov.kw EPA pages cover industrial procedures, chemical company registration and release requests. These are state portal services; no 2026 rule or small-firm recurring duty found. Nothing new.
